assumptions: That the affected requests represent purchase attempts. Nothing in the available evidence links the failed requests to orders, carts, or revenue; the connection rests entirely on the flag and code path being named 'checkout'.

That the disruption began at 21:40 UTC when the flag started rolling and ended at 21:47 when it was restored. The alert fired at 21:45, so roughly five minutes of impact preceded detection and is inferred from the log error-rate warnings rather than from the alert window.

That the service-wide error rate quoted in the alert and the much higher per-minute rate seen in the account-page logs are consistent, i.e. the account page is a minority slice of total traffic and was failing at a far higher rate than the service as a whole. This was not verified against traffic-share data.

That the flag rollback is a mask, not a fix. The alternative reading the investigator recorded — that the division-by-zero defect was already latent in the primary path — is treated here as correct, since no deploy was recorded in the prior 24 hours. It was never tested directly.

That no orders were partially processed or corrupted. The error occurs as an unhandled exception on the request, which suggests failure before any state change, but this was not confirmed against payment or order records.
input.executive_summary: On the evening of 2 September 2026, a configuration switch was flipped on the online shop that moved customers off a known-good checkout path and onto a newer one. The newer path had a bug that made it fail immediately, so customers who reached checkout from their account page got an error instead of being able to complete their purchase. The failures began around 21:40 UTC, alerting fired at 21:45, and the switch was put back to its previous setting at 21:47, after which the service returned to its normal behaviour. Total customer-visible disruption was roughly seven minutes; the automated alert-to-resolution window was about one minute. Only the checkout flow was affected — the rest of the shop continued to work normally, and no data was lost. The underlying bug is still present in the code and is currently only hidden by the configuration setting, so a code fix and a test that exercises the non-fallback path are needed before that flag is turned off again.
input.impact_weight_reason: The failing path is the checkout path itself — the log lines name a checkout fallback flag and the failure is a hard error on the request, not a slow or degraded response — so a customer hitting it could not complete a purchase at that moment. That places it near the top of the scale. It is held below 1.0 for two reasons visible in the evidence: the requests are logged as account-page requests rather than a standalone checkout endpoint, so some share of that traffic is likely account browsing that merely exercises the same code rather than an in-progress purchase; and the outage lasted only a few minutes, which is short enough that a meaningful fraction of blocked buyers would plausibly have retried and converted. Both of those are judgements, not measurements — no conversion or order data was available.
input.root_cause: The `legacy-checkout-fallback` feature flag was turned off, which routed account-page checkout requests onto the primary (non-fallback) code path. That path contains a latent division-by-zero defect, so nearly every request it served raised a ZeroDivisionError. No deploy is recorded in the preceding 24 hours; the flag flip was the trigger, and the defective code was already in production behind the flag.
